record.title: Switzerland expands pandemic entry restrictions at neighbouring frontiers
record.scope: Entry restrictions on four neighbouring frontiers
record.exceptions: Swiss citizens, residents, professional/necessary travel, goods and permitted transit
record.enforcement: Official operational or policy record; independent observation not established unless specified.
record.consequences: Not independently established in this pass
record.relationship: National category regime with staged frontier onset; 15 June is not unrestricted admission of every nationality.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no status extrapolation to 21 October 2026
record.context: See scope and source notes; national restrictions are recorded once, not once per neighbouring country.
record.uncertainty: Swiss government retrospect confirms internal-Schengen reopening and EU/EFTA/UK free movement on 15 June, including the Italian frontier, not just Germany/Austria/France. Third-country short visits remained restricted; onset was staged (Italy 13 March, others 16 March). No independently witnessed first passage at every post; Liechtenstein initial restriction remains unresolved.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Official chronology imposes admission restrictions, beyond checks.
Italy March13; Germany/Austria/France March16, as stated in chronology.
June15 Schengen/free-movement relaxation supported by indexed government retrospective; short third-country tourism remained prohibited.

Four large neighbours; citizens/residents/work/transit/goods and necessity exemptions; no separately confirmed Liechtenstein onset.
Staged territory and category changes; retain no single interval.
